{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with multiple PROs and labs",
      "quote": "PRO/QOL assessments: FACT-G GP5 and PRO- CTCAE",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Cycle 1 Day 1 includes numerous procedures: physical exam, vital signs, labs (chemistry, hematology, urinalysis, pregnancy test), and multiple PROs (FACT-G, PRO-CTCAE, BPI, QLQ-C, QLQ-LC, PGIS, EQ-5D-5L). This is a heavy burden for patients on their first treatment day.",
      "fix": "Consider moving some PROs (e.g., PGIS, EQ-5D-5L) to a separate visit or reducing frequency."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECG only at screening, missing on-treatment assessments",
      "quote": "ECG | X |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ECG is only performed at screening, but the protocol text (Section 8.2.3.2) describes ECG procedures without specifying frequency. For a study with potential cardiac effects, on-treatment ECGs are typically needed.",
      "fix": "Add ECG at specified treatment cycles or as clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Coagulation only at screening and safety follow-up",
      "quote": "Coagulation | X |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Coagulation is only tested at screening and safety follow-up, but it may be needed during treatment to monitor for bleeding or thrombotic events, especially with chemotherapy.",
      "fix": "Add coagulation at least once during treatment cycles."
    },
    {
      "title": "CT/MRI only at screening, no on-treatment tumor assessments",
      "quote": "CT/MRIf | X |  |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The Schedule of Activities shows CT/MRI only at screening, but efficacy assessments require periodic tumor imaging to evaluate response. This is a critical omission.",
      "fix": "Add CT/MRI at specified intervals (e.g., every 6-8 weeks) during treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "PGIC only at Cycle 4, not at baseline",
      "quote": "PRO/QOL assessments: PGIC |  |  |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PGIC (Patient Global Impression of Change) is only administered at Cycle 4 Day 1, but it should be measured relative to baseline. Without a baseline assessment, change cannot be interpreted.",
      "fix": "Add PGIC at baseline or clarify that it is only for subjects who have received treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "PGIS not collected at Cycle 2 and 3",
      "quote": "PRO/QOL assessments: PGIS | X | X |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PGIS is collected at screening, Cycle 1, Cycle 4, and safety follow-up, but not at Cycles 2 and 3. This creates gaps in severity data during early treatment.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting PGIS at each cycle for consistency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Cholesterol and Triglyceride not at baseline",
      "quote": "Cholesterol and Triglyceride |  | X |  | X |  | X |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Cholesterol and Triglyceride are first measured at Cycle 1 Day 1, not at screening. Baseline values are needed to interpret changes.",
      "fix": "Add these tests at screening."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs and labs at every visit including safety follow-up",
      "quote": "Vital signs including oxygen saturation | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and labs (chemistry, hematology, urinalysis, pregnancy test) are performed at every visit, including safety follow-up. This is burdensome for patients, especially at follow-up when they may be off treatment.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing frequency of some labs at follow-up visits."
    }
  ]
}
